summary: Unsafe Git shapes, linked-worktree identity drift, nested-card ambiguity and stale release grants remain fail closed before material state change.
facts: git add -A, option injection, symlink alias, parent escape, foreign repository, commit --amend and custom-strategy merge all resolve to protected metadata and are denied.
A real merge carrying unsupported -m syntax was denied at PreToolUse with no merge state; the equivalent safe --no-ff --no-edit form then succeeded.
A pre-commit installer grant was invalidated when git index blob identity changed; no install state changed until a new current-tree one-shot grant was approved.
Nested continuation action prose is accepted only below the decision-card top level; a conflicting top-level action still fails.
